skill.summary: Review JSON output batches against a limited schema subset and interpret validation errors with clear safety boundaries.

content.user_title: Check JSON Outputs Against a Shared Contract
content.value_statement: API responses and AI-agent outputs can violate expected contracts. This skill guides batch checks against a documented schema subset and explains validation errors.
actual_capabilities: Request a schema and representative JSON outputs while reminding users to redact sensitive data.
Explain the supported validation keywords before interpreting PASS or FAIL results.
Guide batch validation through the linked companion browser tool.
Interpret reported JSON Pointer paths and distinguish syntax errors from contract mismatches.
Suggest minimal schema or payload corrections when the intended contract is clear.
Explain the companion tool's local JUnit XML export and its CI integration boundaries.
limitations: The companion tool accepts one JSON value per non-empty line and only object or array schema nodes.
The subset excludes references, schema composition, format checks, boolean schemas, and schema-valued additionalProperties; unknown keywords are ignored.
Patterns use browser JavaScript regular expressions; PASS covers supported rules only, not full JSON Schema compliance.
This prompt-only skill includes no validator implementation; it does not run CI jobs or upload artifacts.

use_cases.title: Review API response batches
use_cases.description: Compare redacted response samples against an agreed contract and understand reported field mismatches.

use_cases.title: Check structured agent outputs
use_cases.description: Review representative agent outputs for missing fields, incorrect types, and disallowed values within the supported subset.

use_cases.title: Prepare contract test results
use_cases.description: Interpret batch failures and understand how locally exported JUnit XML can inform a separate CI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start a contract check
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check these redacted JSON outputs against this schema: [schema and samples]. Explain the supported subset before interpreting results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a small set of sample outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain validation failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these reported validation errors: [errors and JSON Pointer paths]. Separate syntax errors from contract mismatches using this schema and redacted samples: [inputs].

prompt_templates.title: Suggest minimal corrections
prompt_templates.prompt: The intended contract is [requirements]. Review [schema, redacted payloads, and errors]. Suggest minimal corrections and flag unsupported keywords before interpreting PASS results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: resolve contract mismatches without changing intended requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan CI integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this schema and redacted batch: [inputs]. Identify subset limitations and explain local JUnit XML export for [CI platform]. Do not run jobs or upload artifacts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a separate CI integration workflow.

output_examples.input: A required integer field named count contains the text three. The validator reports a mismatch at /count.
output: Contract mismatch at /count: count must be an integer.
The payload is syntactically valid JSON.
If the intended value is three, replace the text with the integer 3.

output_examples.input: A batch passes, but its schema uses format to require email addresses.
output: The supported subset does not check format.
PASS does not establish that the email addresses are valid.
Use a full validator for production or security-critical contracts.

output_examples.input: A quality assurance engineer wants the browser tool to run CI and publish the batch results.
output: The companion tool supports local JUnit XML export.
It does not run CI jobs or upload artifacts.
Configure execution and artifact handling separately in your CI system.

best_practices: Redact secrets, personal data, and confidential production payloads before sharing samples or using the companion tool.
Check supported keywords before interpreting results, and provide one JSON value per non-empty line.
Clarify the intended contract before changing inputs, and use a full validator for production or security-critical checks.
anti_patterns: Treating PASS as complete JSON Schema compliance or a security guarantee.
Relying on ignored keywords, references, or schema composition to enforce contract requirements.
Weakening a schema merely to eliminate failures without confirming the intended contract.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a JSON Schema and representative redacted outputs. For the companion tool, place one JSON value on each non-empty line.

faq.question: Which schema rules are supported?
faq.answer: Supported keywords are type, required, properties, additionalProperties=false, items, enum, const, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minItems, and maxItems.

faq.question: Does PASS mean full JSON Schema compliance?
faq.answer: No. PASS covers only supported rules. Unknown keywords are ignored, and references, composition, format checks, and boolean schemas are unsupported.

faq.question: Does the companion tool upload my inputs?
faq.answer: The skill states that the browser tool processes inputs locally without uploads. The tool implementation was not reviewed; redact sensitive data before use.

faq.question: Can this skill run my CI pipeline?
faq.answer: No. It explains local JUnit XML export from the companion tool. CI execution and artifact uploads require a separate workflow.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill provides instructions rather than a bundled executable validator.
